failures.evidence: packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md:1314-1319 (round 2's precondition) says a test 'stays untagged, whatever its title says, when it ... sets a desktop viewport for every project before it checks anything'. e2e/issue.e2e.ts:1226 'the details rail fades its trailing edge only while it has somewhere to scroll @phone' (table v2 keep row issue.e2e.ts:1238, R3/R5/R6) matches that clause as written: :1229 test.skip(testInfo.project.name !== "iphone"), then :1241 page.setViewportSize({ height: 900, width: 1920 }) unconditionally, then expect(rail).toBeVisible() and the overflow/mask checks at 1920, and only then 390. So an author who applies the rule untags it, and it then runs nowhere: in a scratch copy of 2cd0e103 with ' @phone' removed from its title, `bunx playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts --list -g "the details rail fades"` lists '[chromium] › issue.e2e.ts:1226:1 › …' and 'Total: 1 test in 1 file', no [iphone] row, and its own skip at :1229 stops it under chromium. R5 ('runs only on the phone') tags it, but the precondition is read first and says the R rules do not apply. My scan (bun $TMPDIR/infra521-test/precond.ts over the head e2e tree, tagged tests with a non-chromium skip or a first setViewportSize of 768 px or wider, each hit read by hand) finds this the only tagged test the precondition reaches as written: every other hit sets the desktop viewport only under `project.name === "chromium"` or `!isPhone` (R1), or sets a phone width first. No red test is possible: the defect is in AGENTS.md prose, and a test that reads that text is a source-text test, which the repository's test rules forbid. Fix belongs to the implementer, e.g. the precondition excludes a test that runs only on `iphone` (R5), or clause two reads 'on chromium and iphone alike'.
